# Does a spot-aware planner (nests, lairs, whetstone, dogs, paid crates) give more power early than the default?

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Status | done |
| Area | spots |
| Result | refuted |
| Created | L2.I2 |
| Updated | L2.I3 |

## Hypothesis

Giving the planner {{spots}}, {{elites}} and {{schedule}} and a goal prompt that rates free-power spots above exploring and evading gets more chests, weapon levels and dogs by 2:30, and a longer life than the default planner on the same seeds.

## Method

Seeker-sprouts from 0:00 on seeds 31, 32 and 33, 300 s. Compare each game with the seeker baseline game on the same seed (L2.I1.G1-G3). Read chests opened, spots used by kind, dogs, gold spent, health at 3:00 and death time.

## Findings

L2.I2: seeker-sprouts on seeds 31, 32 and 33, 300 s. The spot-aware arm died at 1:44, 1:34 and 0:59 against baselines of 3:23, 3:08 and 0:52. No seed lived longer. Seed 32 opened 4 chests by 1:34 but died to Cave Grubs. Only one 30-gold paid crate was bought per game. Spots-first as written is not worth adopting.
